_about: beast-recipe's engine and family capability matrix: which engine build reads which model_type in which checkpoint format, at which rank counts (TP = Sparks, one rank per Spark), how it is launched, and what work stands between a model and a served endpoint. DATA: read by scripts/backends/pylib/recipe.py, never executed. docs/BEAST_RECIPE.md 'The engine and family matrix' explains every field and how to update it. Every engine and family names its source and the date it was read; labels follow the investigation: VERIFIED (read on a primary source), CLAIMED (a README, changelog or model card), ESTIMATED (our arithmetic).
_sources: scripts/backends/data/spark-families.json (the families the pair serves today)

spark.source: MemTotal 127,598,412 kB on each Spark (MEASURED); the intake rule W <= 92 fits, 92-100 tight, > 100 no (spark-families.json pair); replicated share 0.008 calibrated on DeepSeek's rank file (0.5039 of the checkpoint at TP2); OS + command center ~6 GiB on the head, 2-3 on a worker (MEASURED 2026-11-17); memguard kills a rank under 2.5 GiB for 4 s

topologies.1: one Spark, no fabric; on the pair today that means the pair's model is down (both Sparks are taken by it)
topologies.2: one QSFP cable, both PCIe twins as two RoCE rails (today: spark-1 + spark-2)
topologies.3: a cabled triangle, one subnet per cable (GLM TP3 measured by Mia's Python recipe v1.5; CLAIMED)
topologies.4: a cabled ring (GLM 1104 start-tp4-switchless.sh, CLAIMED) or a 200 GbE RoCE switch; spark-cluster.sh check does not know the ring yet
topologies.5-8: a 200/400 GbE RoCE switch (community CRS812 builds; CLAIMED)

hardware.buy: each added Spark: one DGX Spark + its QSFP cables (two more Sparks and two more cables make the 4-ring; no switch needed for 4)
